key_insight: Nondimensionalization and a variational inequality FEM formulation make a stiff morphoelastic burn-healing model computationally tractable while revealing that higher-order parameter interactions dominate key outcomes.
engineering_relevance: The framework improves solver robustness for biomechanical healing simulations and helps identify which biological and mechanical parameters most influence wound contraction and contracture.
method: Nondimensionalize the governing equations to simplify the coupled bio-mechanical system
Use scaling analysis to justify neglecting chemotaxis and inertia, enabling a quasi-static momentum model
Implement non-negativity constraints with a Variational Inequality FEM approach in FEniCSx
evidence_signal: The study validates the approach with convergence studies, mass-balance checks, and a sensitivity analysis spanning nearly four million simulations.
watch_item: The model’s predictive behavior appears to depend on higher-order interactions, so interpretation and calibration may be sensitive and pairwise analyses alone can miss key effects.
paper_title: Nondimensionalization, Variational Inequalities and Uncertainty Quantification in a Morphoelastic Model for Burn Injury Healing
